title: AWS Lambda and serverless compute patterns — concept map
intro: Lambda executes handlers in ephemeral sandboxes scaled by AWS. Cold starts initialize runtime; warm invocations reuse environment until frozen. VPC access creates ENIs. Triggers connect S3, API Gateway, SQS, EventBridge, and more. Concurrency caps and DLQs handle failure modes. Compare with long-running EC2 and containerized Fargate for sustained load.

overviewDiagram.source:
flowchart LR

  L --> E[Execution environment]
  E --> H[Handler code]
  E --> VPC[VPC ENI optional]
  H --> AWS[AWS SDK calls]
  L --> DLQ[DLQ on async failure]

conceptCards.title: Execution env
conceptCards.summary: Frozen container reuse; /tmp 512MB–10GB; state not guaranteed across invocations.
conceptCards.example: Reuse SDK client outside handler for warm perf

conceptCards.title: Cold starts
conceptCards.summary: Init runtime + handler load. Provisioned concurrency keeps environments warm.

conceptCards.title: VPC Lambda
conceptCards.summary: Hyperplane ENIs in subnets for RDS access. Needs NAT or endpoints for AWS APIs.

conceptCards.title: Triggers
conceptCards.summary: Sync vs async invoke. Event source mappings poll SQS/Kinesis.
conceptCards.example: S3 ObjectCreated async with retry + DLQ

conceptCards.title: Concurrency & DLQ
conceptCards.summary: Account and function reserved concurrency. Async failures to DLQ after retries.

conceptCards.title: vs EC2/Fargate
conceptCards.summary: Lambda for event-driven burst; EC2/Fargate for steady TCP, long jobs, custom kernel.
conceptCards.example: WebSocket server on EC2 not Lambda
